name: Oat and honey calming mask
blurb: A soothing mask for dry, tight, or easily upset skin. Mix it fresh for one use.
steps: Stir the oatmeal and honey together.
Add water a little at a time until it's a spreadable paste.
Apply to clean skin, leave 10 minutes, then rinse with lukewarm water.

name: Barrier face oil
blurb: A light, gentle face oil with a trace of lavender. Leave out the lavender for very sensitive skin.
steps: Sanitize a 30 ml dark glass dropper bottle.
Add the oils, vitamin E, and lavender. Cap and roll gently to mix.
Use 2 to 3 drops on damp skin at night.
keeps: About 3 months in the fridge, because of the rosehip.

name: Whipped shea body butter
blurb: A rich, fluffy butter for dry elbows, knees, and legs.
steps: Melt the shea and mango butter gently over a water bath.
Stir in the sunflower oil and vitamin E, then chill until soft-set (about 30 minutes).
Add the lavender and whip with a hand mixer for 3 to 5 minutes until fluffy.
Spoon into a clean jar.
keeps: 6 to 12 months if kept dry. Use a clean spoon, not wet hands.

name: Beeswax lip balm
blurb: A simple, unscented balm. Fills about four small tubes.
steps: Melt the beeswax and shea over a water bath.
Take off the heat, stir in the oil and vitamin E.
Pour into tubes or tins and let set at room temperature.

name: Brown sugar body scrub
blurb: A softening body scrub. Use in the shower on dry patches, never on the face.
steps: Mix the sugar and oil in a clean bowl.
Stir in the sweet orange oil.
Pack into a jar with a tight lid.
keeps: About 6 months. Keep shower water out of the jar and scoop with a dry spoon.

name: Kaolin clay mask powder
blurb: A dry mix you keep in a jar and wet one spoonful at a time. Suits normal and combination skin.
steps: Mix the powders and store in a dry, sealed jar.
For one mask, mix 1 tsp powder with 1 to 2 tsp distilled water or hydrosol.
Apply, and rinse after 8 to 10 minutes before it cracks.

name: Rhassoul hammam mask
blurb: The clay step from a Moroccan hammam routine. Suits normal to oily skin.
steps: Stir the clay and rose water into a smooth paste.
Spread over clean skin, avoiding the eyes.
Rinse with warm water after 5 to 10 minutes, before it cracks, then moisturize.
keeps: Single use. Keep the dry clay in a sealed jar.

name: Classic sugaring paste
blurb: The traditional three-ingredient hair removal paste. Full method and temperatures are on the Sugaring tab.
steps: Stir everything over medium heat until the sugar dissolves.
Stop stirring once it boils and cook to 245–250°F (118–121°C), honey to amber in color.
Pour into a heat-safe jar and cool until warm and pliable. Test on your wrist before use.
keeps: Several months sealed at room temperature.
